question.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})=-\frac{1}{2}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is ${x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{6} & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 2x-\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{7\pi }{6}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{4\pi }{3}+2n\pi  \\ x & =n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+\frac{3n\pi }{3} \\ x & =n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(2+3n)\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=0$ and $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\pi $ and $x=\frac{5\pi }{3}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=0,\frac{2\pi }{3},\pi ,\frac{5\pi }{3}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and ${x}_{3}=\pi ,$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3}+\pi =\frac{2\pi }{3}+\frac{3\pi }{3}=\frac{5\pi }{3}.
$$
